## Role and Cost Boundary

An offshore HVDC converter station changes the wind farm's collected AC power to DC for export. A second station onshore changes it back to grid-compatible AC. This page owns the converter electrical equipment at both terminals, but not the offshore support structure or its installation.

| Physical scope | Treatment | Cost owner |
|---|---|---|
| Offshore and onshore converter valves | Included | **This page** |
| Converter transformers, reactors, cooling and auxiliaries | Included | **This page** |
| Immediate AC/DC switchgear, control and protection | Included | **This page** |
| Offshore platform and foundation | Reference only | [Platform Material CAPEX](../platforms/platform_material_capex.qmd) |
| Platform transport and offshore installation | Reference only | [Platform and Substation Installation](../offshore_installation/platform_and_substation_installation.qmd) |
| HVDC cable supply and installation | Excluded | [HVDC Export Cables](hvdc_export_cables.qmd) and [Cable and Pipeline Installation](../offshore_installation/cable_and_pipeline_installation.qmd) |
| Wider onshore grid reinforcement | Excluded | [Onshore Grid Connection](onshore_grid_connection.qmd) |

<span class="cost-reference">Green = booked on this page</span>
<span class="cost-reference">Grey = reference only; not booked on this page</span>

## Reference Configuration

The electrical design reference is TenneT's 2 GW North Sea standard [@tennet2024TwoGWProgram; @tennet2025TwoGWStandard]:

| Parameter | Reference value |
|---|---:|
| Rated active-power transfer | 2 GW |
| Offshore collection voltage | 66 kV AC |
| Converter technology | VSC using modular multilevel converters |
| HVDC configuration | Bipole with dedicated metallic return |
| Pole voltage | +/-525 kV |
| Offshore generation blocks | 4 x 500 MW |
| Offshore HVDC transformers | Four |
| Onshore grid voltage | 380 kV AC |
| Normal full-load pole current | 1.905 kA |
| Healthy-pole degraded transfer | Approximately 1 GW |

For balanced bipolar operation:

$$
P_\mathrm{dc}=2V_\mathrm{pole}I_\mathrm{pole}.
$$

At 2 GW and 525 kV per pole, $I_\mathrm{pole}=1.905$ kA. The converter MVA rating must additionally cover reactive-power duty, voltage range, harmonics, overloads and grid-code margins.

## Converter Cost Model

### DEA Basis

The Danish Energy Agency gives a 2025 central planning value of 320 EUR/kW for an onshore 525 kV DC converter station, with 250--420 EUR/kW as its low and high cases. These values are stated at the 2020 price level [@danishEnergyAgency2025Transport].

The report's factor of 1.263 restates 2020 values through forecast 2026 inflation. For the common EUR~2025~ basis, the 3.0% forecast 2026 step is removed explicitly:

$$
F_{2020\rightarrow2025}
=
\frac{1.263}{1.030}
=
1.22621.
$$

The transformation uses euro-area annual-average HICP through 2025 and the European Commission's 3.0% euro-area inflation forecast for 2026 [@eurostat2026HICP; @europeanCommission2026Forecast].

The DEA offshore-station value includes its platform, so it cannot be booked as
converter equipment alongside a separate platform cost. No executable converter
pair price is adopted here. Earlier paired coefficients are retained in the audit
baseline rather than presented as active inputs. Equipment-only scope, price
normalisation and an executable electricity branch remain unresolved.

## Complete Station-Cost Perspective

The physical offshore station also needs a platform, foundation, transport and installation. Those costs are useful context but are not booked on this page.

| Cost-stack element | Reference value | Status | Cost owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Offshore + onshore converter equipment | Unresolved | No adopted executable input | **This page** |
| Offshore platform and offshore premium proxy | <span class="cost-reference">527 EUR~2025~/kW</span> | DEA offshore-minus-onshore difference; not an adopted standalone platform cost | [Platform Material CAPEX](../platforms/platform_material_capex.qmd) |
| Platform offshore installation | <span class="cost-reference">TBD</span> | Must be separated from fabrication and equipment | [Platform and Substation Installation](../offshore_installation/platform_and_substation_installation.qmd) |
| DEA offshore + onshore station pair, platform included | <span class="cost-reference">1,312 EUR~2025~/kW</span> | Scope comparator, not added to the rows above | [Platform Material CAPEX](../platforms/platform_material_capex.qmd) |

::: {.callout-note}
## Reference costs are not additional costs

The grey values show the complete physical context. Their derivation, uncertainty and booking rules are maintained on the linked pages. No converter price on this page is currently booked by an electricity scenario.
:::

Public TenneT programme announcements correspond to roughly EUR 1,000--1,170/kW when divided by announced system count and rating [@tennet2gwProgrammeData; @hitachiPetrofac2023TenneT; @geVernova2023TenneT; @siemensEnergy2023TenneT]. These are broad infrastructure-package comparisons, not converter-only prices. Their scopes are more comparable with the DEA offshore-plus-onshore station range, which includes the platform, than with a converter-equipment-only scope.

## Conversion Losses

Converter-station losses cover power electronics, transformers, reactors,
cooling and auxiliaries. No flat station efficiency is adopted for the current
model. Supplier curves and an explicitly scoped input are required before an
executable electricity result can be produced. Equipment examples and earlier
working assumptions are retained in the audit baseline; they do not set losses
for the hydrogen branches.

## Availability and Degraded Operation

No flat terminal availability is adopted. A future capacity-state model would distinguish:

| State | Available export capacity | Example cause |
|---|---:|---|
| Both poles and terminals healthy | 2 GW | Normal operation |
| One pole path unavailable | Approximately 1 GW | Pole converter, transformer or cable outage |
| Both poles unavailable | 0 GW | Common control, auxiliary or platform event |

Capacity-weighted availability is:

$$
A_E
=
1-
\frac{\sum_i\Delta P_i\Delta t_i}
{P_\mathrm{rated}T}.
$$

Once these states are simulated, the corresponding flat availability factors must be removed.

## Current Assumptions

| Parameter | Base case | Sensitivity or next step | Evidence status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Link rating | 2 GW reference | Test discrete link count | Public TenneT standard |
| Pole voltage | +/-525 kV | Fixed for reference design | Public TenneT standard |
| Converter pair CAPEX, platform excluded | Unresolved | Equipment-only scope and adopted price basis required | Reference evidence is not an active cost |
| Scaling | Linear up to 2 GW | Use complete links above 2 GW | Screening assumption |
| Offshore aggregate efficiency | Unresolved | Replace with supplier loss curve | Conservative working value |
| Onshore aggregate efficiency | Unresolved | Replace with supplier loss curve | Conservative working value |
| Station availability | Unresolved | Future capacity-state work deferred | No flat value adopted |
| Converter OPEX | TBD | Obtain equipment-specific basis | Not supplied by CAPEX source |

## Model Limitations

| Limitation | Implication |
|---|---|
| Offshore converter uses the onshore cost coefficient | Offshore marinisation and logistics premium are not represented in converter CAPEX |
| Platform and installation costs remain incompletely separated | The complete offshore-station cost is not yet a fully additive bottom-up estimate |
| HICP is a general price index | HVDC equipment escalation may differ from consumer inflation |
| Linear EUR/kW scaling | Discrete equipment and platform thresholds are hidden |
| Constant station efficiencies | Part-load, no-load and temperature effects are hidden |
| Flat terminal availabilities | Pole redundancy and common-mode failures are simplified |

Complete central-platform mass is estimated separately on the [Complete Topside Mass](../platforms/topside_mass.qmd) page. Its aggregate reference already includes hosted equipment; component masses are not added again.
